Let
\[
U=t^2+4xy
\]
and
\[
W=z(Ht+2Ey+2Fx)+\frac12\,t(pq+qp)-yp^2+xq^2 .
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k[z,\;t^2+4xy,\;z(Ht+2Ey+2Fx)+\tfrac12t(pq+qp)-yp^2+xq^2].}
\]

Here is the proof.

Since \(z\) is central, localize at \(z\). In \(R[z^{-1}]\), define
\[
E_0=E-\frac{p^2}{2z},\qquad
F_0=F+\frac{q^2}{2z},\qquad
H_0=H+\frac{pq+qp}{2z}.
\]
A direct use of \(pq-qp=z\) gives
\[
[E_0,p]=[E_0,q]=[F_0,p]=[F_0,q]=[H_0,p]=[H_0,q]=0.
\]
Also \(E_0,F_0,H_0\) still satisfy the \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) relations and act on \(x,t,y\) exactly as \(E,F,H\) do. Therefore
\[
R[z^{-1}]
\cong A_z\otimes U(\mathfrak{sl}_2\ltimes V),
\]
where \(A_z\) is the localized Heisenberg/Weyl algebra generated by \(p,q,z^{\pm1}\), and \(V=kx\oplus kt\oplus ky\) is the adjoint \(3\)-dimensional \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-module.

The center of \(A_z\) is \(k[z,z^{-1}]\). For the Takiff algebra \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\ltimes V\), with \(V\) abelian and adjoint, the center of its enveloping algebra is
\[
k[U,C],
\]
where
\[
U=t^2+4xy,\qquad C=H_0t+2E_0y+2F_0x.
\]
Indeed, \(U\) is the basic quadratic invariant on the adjoint copy \(V\), and
\[
C=H_0t+2E_0y+2F_0x
\]
commutes with \(x,t,y\) because
\[
[C,x]=(2xt-2xt)=0,\quad [C,y]=(-2yt+2ty)=0,\quad [C,t]=(-4xy+4xy)=0,
\]
and it commutes with \(E_0,F_0,H_0\) by the same adjoint-invariance calculation. Conversely, the PBW filtration reduces any central element to an invariant polynomial for \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\ltimes V\), and that invariant ring is generated by the two pairings \(U\) and \(C\). Hence
\[
Z(R[z^{-1}])=k[z,z^{-1},U,C].
\]

Substituting back,
\[
zC
=z(Ht+2Ey+2Fx)+\frac12t(pq+qp)-yp^2+xq^2
=W.
\]
Thus
\[
Z(R[z^{-1}])=k[z,z^{-1},U,W/z].
\]
Intersecting with the original, nonlocalized algebra \(R\) removes negative powers of \(z\). Since the image of \(W\) modulo \(z\) is
\[
\tfrac12t(pq+qp)-yp^2+xq^2,
\]
which is not divisible by \(z\), no nontrivial negative power of \(z\) can occur in an element of \(R\). Therefore
\[
Z(R)=k[z,U,W].
\]

So explicitly,
\[
\boxed{
Z(R)=k\!\left[
z,\;
t^2+4xy,\;
z(Ht+2Ey+2Fx)+\frac12t(pq+qp)-yp^2+xq^2
\right].
}
\]
